evidence: Wikipedia's article on 'Blue Monday': the rhythm was programmed on an Oberheim DMX drum machine, with a Moog Source for the bass line, synchronised by a circuit Bernard Sumner built because MIDI did not yet exist.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: The famous opening is the DMX on its own: a kick drum firing in a stuttering sixteenth-note burst, then settling into a steady beat. Listen for how mechanical and exact it is, and how it keeps going unchanged under everything else. That opening is why DJs played it.

explanation.age13: 'Blue Monday' starts with a drum machine, an Oberheim DMX, playing a fast, stuttering kick drum. Bernard Sumner built his own gadget to keep it in time with the synthesizers, because the standard way of connecting them didn't exist yet.
explanation.adult: A technological edge with a specific, well-known sound attached. The home-made sync circuit is part of the story: it is what a band had to build to make machines play together before MIDI.
